title: Find Customers Who Have Never Placed an Order
description:
Find all customers who have **never** placed any order by using a LEFT JOIN and checking for NULL on the right side.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `amount`

Output columns: `name`, `email`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@x.com'),(2,'Bob','bob@x.com'),(3,'Carol','carol@x.com'),(4,'Dave','dave@x.com'),(5,'Eve','eve@x.com'),(6,'Frank','frank@x.com'),(7,'Grace','grace@x.com'),(8,'Henry','henry@x.com'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, amount DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,100.00),(2,2,200.00),(3,2,150.00),(4,4,80.00),(5,6,300.00),(6,8,90.00);
solution_sql: SELECT c.name, c.email FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.customer_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name

test_cases.description: 8 customers; customers 1,2,4,6,8 have orders; customers 3 (Carol), 5 (Eve), 7 (Grace) have none — 3 rows

hints: LEFT JOIN keeps all customers regardless of whether they have orders; the order columns will be NULL for customers with no match.
WHERE o.customer_id IS NULL filters to only those unmatched customers — the anti-join pattern.
explanation: LEFT JOIN returns all 8 customers. For customers who have orders (1,2,4,6,8) the orders columns are populated. For customers 3, 5, and 7 there are no matching orders, so all order columns are NULL. WHERE o.customer_id IS NULL keeps only these NULL rows — 3 unmatched customers. This is the standard anti-join pattern.
